## Today's Forecast
Isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms are expected today with daytime highs reaching 31°C / 88°F and overnight lows near 19°C / 67°F. Thunder possible from midday, peaking this afternoon. Rainfall totals around 2.2 mm (0.09 in) are expected, with the primary onset window between 13:00 and 15:00. Skies will remain mostly cloudy across the early hours, midday, and evening. Surface winds will turn north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday and south into the evening, with peak gusts reaching 39 km/h (21 kt) ashore. Solar UV exposure peaks at a maximum UV index of 9.4. Ground air quality monitoring stations report a range from 34 to 42, with the worst reading at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, while broader model estimates indicate an AQI of 72.

## Extended Outlook
Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Mostly cloudy skies are expected on Thursday, October 8, transitioning to partly cloudy on Friday, October 9, and returning to mostly cloudy on Saturday, October 10. High temperatures on Saturday will range from 29°C / 84°F to 35°C / 95°F due to model spread. From Sunday, October 11, through Wednesday, October 14, conditions remain unsettled under mostly cloudy skies with continued daily precipitation potential and lower forecast confidence.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability is significant today, though models differ on its strength: GFS shows minimal CAPE near 320 J/kg, ECMWF, ICON, and Best Match build moderate instability between 1720 J/kg and 2370 J/kg, and UKMO peaks at 3440 J/kg CAPE. Any developing thunderstorm poses a localized hazard of sudden, strong wind gusts generated by convective downdrafts, regardless of background wind forecasts.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Over-water wind conditions will follow a timeline of northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 12 km/h (6 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 22 km/h (12 kt), then southerly into the evening at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt). Peak gusts across the Gulf will reach 31 km/h (17 kt). Boaters should stay alert for rapid wind shifts and sudden gust spikes near convective showers.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Across the Nyanza Basin, regional mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.8 hPa and 1015.0 hPa, with weak pressure gradients favoring afternoon lake-breeze convergence and moisture buildup over the basin.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
At Day+0, model track record verification reflects a settled sample (56 checks) showing no single model holding a statistically established ranking advantage over the rest. GFS maintains an established warm bias on daytime highs (predicting 33.5°C today), whereas ECMWF and ICON forecast cooler highs near 29.1°C to 29.6°C; today's forecaster call high of 31.1°C sits between these two guidance clusters. Kenya Meteorological Department published a forecast for Kisumu calling for a high of 32.0°C / 90°F and a low of 20.0°C / 68°F with light showers and thunderstorms expected. All numerical models under-forecast peak gusts at Day+0, supporting the calibrated gust adjustment to 39.3 km/h ashore. Ground air quality sensors reported fresh data: Kisumu Airport at AQI 36 (PM2.5 36.0 µg/m³, PM10 15.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue at AQI 42 (PM2.5 42.0 µg/m³, PM10 18.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach at AQI 34 (PM2.5 34.0 µg/m³, PM10 37.0 µg/m³).
